gloss: Being a friend to all beings is the first mark of the one dear to God, according to the Gita (12.13). Goodwill and friendliness are the qualities of maitrī.

hero.m: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
hero.sa: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥

loci.m: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
loci.sa: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥

loci.m: Jajali, the one who is always a friend to all, devoted to the good of all, in action, thought and word, is the one who truly knows dharma.
loci.sa: सर्वेषां यः सुहृन्नित्यं सर्वेषां च हिते रतः / कर्मणा मनसा वाचा स धर्मं वेद जाजले

loci.m: I am happy when people are happy and sad when people are sad; I am a dear friend to all. So I live long, free of illness.
loci.sa: सुखितोऽस्मि सुखापन्ने दुःखितो दुःखिते जने । सर्वस्य प्रियमित्रं च तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

practices.m: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
practices.sa: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
practices.why: Shows words chosen true, kind and helpful build goodwill.

practices.m: One who, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.
practices.sa: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
practices.why: Shows wishing others' happiness as one's own.

practices.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
practices.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
practices.why: Shows no contempt in talk of others.

practices.m: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
practices.sa: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्
practices.why: Names friendship as the source of every good.

practices.m: Make a friend slowly, and give one up slowly. A friendship made slowly is one that lasts long.
practices.sa: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति
practices.why: Shows slow friendship is the lasting kind.

practices.m: The person who never says a word and always wears a frown is disliked by everyone, for he does not practise kind speech. But the one who notices everyone, speaks to them first, and greets them with a smile, wins the whole world's goodwill.
practices.sa: यो हि नाभाषते किंचित्सर्वदा भुकुटीमुखः / द्वेष्यो भवति भूतानां स सान्त्वमिह नाचरन् यस्तु सर्वमभिप्रेक्ष्य पूर्वमेवाभिभाषते / स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च तस्य लोकः प्रसीदति
practices.why: Shows warm speech as a daily practice.

practices.m: The eight million four hundred thousand kinds of beings, living in water, on land and in the sky: knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Ram, I bow to them with folded hands.
practices.sa: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥

practices.m: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
practices.sa: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥

stories.l: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.
stories.s: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.

stories.l: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.
stories.s: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.

stories.l: Homecoming is about people, not possessions; don't let property come between siblings.
stories.s: Victorious, Ram refuses Lanka's honours: his heart is in a hurry to see Bharata. Near Ayodhya he sends Hanuman ahead to read Bharata's face, saying if Bharata now wants the kingdom, let him keep it.

stories.l: The deepest gratitude hopes the other never needs your help.
stories.s: After the coronation Ram sends his friends home, asking only to be remembered with love. Hanuman asks to live as long as Ram's story is told, so that hearing it can ease his longing. Ram rises from the throne, embraces him, grants it, and says he would give his life for each of Hanuman's services, and hopes Hanuman never falls into trouble that would let him repay it.
stories.t: Valmiki: Hanuman's boon and Ram's debt
